data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB, NHATS), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, data.nasa.gov), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Radio Experiment (REX)
record.mission_name: New Horizons Pluto Kuiper Belt Flyby
record.description: The Radio Experiment (REX) will use the New Horizons telecommunications system with its 2.1 meter antenna to perform radio science and radiometry measurements at Pluto, Charon, and any Kuiper Belt Objects (KBOs) encountered during the mission. During its occultation as it flies behind Pluto as seen from Earth it will make soundings of Pluto's ionospheric density and the atmospheric temperature and pressure down to the surface. It will use a radiometry mode to look for weak radio emissions from Pluto to derive globally averaged values for the dayside and nightside temperatures. It will also search for atmospheres and weak radio emissions at Charon and KBOs. REX will further be used to estimate the masses of Pluto, Charon, and KBOs by tracking small perturbations in the trajectory due to the gravity of the bodies. Improved estimates of the radii of Pluto and Charon will be made by timing the lengths of the radio occultations. REX is consists of a printed circuit board containing signal-processing electronics which is integrated into the telecommunications system. The telecom system is redundant, so the spacecraft has two copies of REX, one in each system. The REX system operates at 4.1 cm and has an effective field of view and angular resolution of 20 milliradians. The signal/noise power spectral density is 55 db-Hz. An ultrastable oscillator gives stability of 1E-13 in 1 second samples. Disk averaged radiometry will give an accuracy of 0.1 K.
